recheck.why:
Independent recheck of E:\code\VLSI\semiskill\skills\dv-signal-trace-localisation\SKILL.md against the three _shared/ files. This is a strong skill — the DV content is the best part of it — but two defects in the retrieval mechanics stop me handing it over, one of them in the seed step.

(1) DOMAIN CORRECTNESS — essentially sound. Spot-checked and correct: the VCD alias/name-map argument; NBA sampling ("A signal that changes at the same timestamp as an active edge was sampled with its old value"); delta-cycle ordering is dump order not causality; the glitch rule with its three real exceptions (async reset, latch, clock gate); X-optimism on conditionals vs X-pessimism on arithmetic; nets optimised away having no values; back-pressure making the guilty side the quiet one. Three nits, none blocking: (a) VCD identifier codes are "one or more printable ASCII" — on a large SoC dump 3- and 4-character aliases are routine, so "keyed by one- and two-character aliases" is narrower than the format; (b) "an X on any operand of an arithmetic or shift operation poisons the whole result" is right for arithmetic but overstated for a shift whose *data* operand carries X — those X bits move positionally rather than poisoning every bit; (c) step 6 splits RTL hits into "the declaration" and "the drivers (its occurrences on the left of an assignment)" and omits the third and, at exactly the module-port bisection boundaries step 6 recommends, the most common case — a net driven by a submodule output port connection (`.dout(sig)`), which is neither a declaration nor an LHS assignment. An agent applying that two-way split literally at a port reports "no driver found".

(2) BUDGET — the arithmetic is exact and honest, but one step cannot be carried out inside it. The stated caps are: log = 1 Grep + 1 x 80-line Read (step 1); export = 6 Greps (3 in step 3, 1 in step 5, 2 spare for step 7) + 4 Reads (1 in step 4, 1 in step 5, 2 spare); RTL = 4 Greps + 3 x 60-line Reads, step 6 only; 3 rounds with a stopping rule. Every Grep the steps actually spend is accounted for, and no step spends an unlisted one. **But the whole retrieval strategy silently assumes one of the two export shapes the skill's own slot contemplates.** Line 47 asks the team for "whether an unchanged value is repeated on every row" — that describes a column-per-signal table, one row per timestamp carrying all signals, which is the standard viewer text listing. Under that shape a Grep on a signal name hits the header line only. Step 5's core move — "**Grep** the export for the suspect signal and take the **earliest** timestamp at which it holds a value the reference forbids" — then returns one header hit and no values, and there is no budgeted way back: the divergence line number is unknown, and 4 x 80-line Reads cover 320 rows of a window that may be thousands. Line 86 ("anchor it with whatever separator the **Export format** slot says surrounds a name") and budget rule 1 ("Grep for a name or a timestamp") both presume the *other* shape, one row per signal per change. Step 3's reset Grep degrades the same way: under a tabular export it proves the reset column exists but cannot show "a window starting inside reset", which is the failure it claims to catch. Nothing in the procedure reconciles the two shapes or tells the reader which branch to take.

(3) UNKNOWABLE ASSERTIONS — clean. Everything tool-, path-, flag- or convention-specific is a slot or a profile reference. The optimised-away gotcha correctly refuses to name a visibility flag ("a flag question for them, never one to guess"). No invented message strings, no invented tool names.

(4) SLOTS — all eight are spent: Waveform database location (steps 2, 3), Dump scope (step 3, gotcha), Export format (steps 2, 3, budget 5, gotcha), Export cost (step 2), Export owner (step 2 handoff), Time unit and radix (steps 1, 2), Clock and reset names (steps 2, 3), RTL source root (step 6). The five claimed profile facts are spent where claimed and every name matches team-profile.md exactly (Log location, Fatal markers, Run identity, Area to owner map, Rerun convention). C001 confirms: the checker's only C001 warning in the pack is on dv-repo-orientation, not this file. The paragraph distinguishing waveform-database location from log location, and Time unit and radix from anything the profile records, is honest and correct.

(5) HANDOFF BLOCK — agrees with handoff-vocabulary.md and is almost fully assigned. `class : design | infrastructure | unknown` is the full registered T1 set with narrowing `no`; `signature`, `run id`, `owner`, `notes` follow their locked shapes; the `mechanism` -> `localised as` rename from the T3 retired row is complete, with no bare "mechanism" left anywhere in the body (grep confirms 0 hits) — that is the rename rule obeyed properly. The claim that "`class`, `run id`, `log` and `notes` are the fields `dv-sim-log-first-error` emits" checks out against that skill's block, as does "both emit a `run id` field". Two residual points: (a) `divergence` is a T3 held-and-unclaimed noun — the registry says "A holder of `-` means the noun is reserved and unclaimed: qualify it before use", and both prior users were renamed away to `view match` and `divergence class`. C010 does not fire because the value here is free text, not a token list, so this is legal by the checker's design — but a reader of the registry meets the word "reserved" and then finds this skill using it bare; `divergence point` or similar would cost one edit. (b) `signature` is offered unconditionally but no step derives one — step 1 only says "If a signature already exists from `dv-sim-log-first-error`, take it as written". The fallback exists in the shared schema, so it is thin rather than broken.

(6) METADATA — `semiskill-role: dv-engineer`, `semiskill-level: senior`. Exactly right. Frontmatter is exactly the ADR-008 key set, review-by 2027-07-29 is ~12 months out and does not collide with dv-sim-log-first-error's 2027-08-05. Length 349 lines is above the 180-260 guidance but squarely at pack norm (82 of 84 skills exceed 260; dv-ral-bringup is 359) — not a finding.

(7) LINT — `python -m semiskill.cli lint skills/dv-signal-trace-localisation` returns `[approve 1.000]  clean`, `1/1 clean - 0 errors - 0 advisories - 1 predicted to publish`. `check_pack` over the whole skills/ tree returns zero findings of any rule for this slug.

(8) THE BLOCKER. Step 1 line 97-99: "Use **one Grep** of the failing log for the **Fatal markers** ..., take the lowest hit, and **Read** one window of about 80 lines *before* it — the only log window this skill spends. Record verbatim the **observation point** ..., the **observation time**, the **expected value** if the message carries one". The window is pointed away from the text the step must record. The golden reference gets this right and this skill drops the load-bearing word: dv-sim-log-first-error step 2 says "Read a window that **starts** about 60 lines *before* it", so its window runs through and past the hit. Here the window lies before the hit, and step 1 has exactly one Grep and one Read with no recovery. The Grep output does carry the marker line itself, so the component and time survive — but the **expected value does not**: the pack's own canonical layout in _shared/failure-signature-schema.md puts it on the *following* line ("UVM_ERROR .../sb.sv(212) @ 141250: ... [MISCOMPARE]" then "expected 0xdeadbeef got 0x00000000 on beat 37"). That line carries no fatal marker, so the Grep misses it and a window "before" the hit cannot reach it. The consequence is not cosmetic: step 5 names "the expected value the check itself printed, recorded in step 1" as the **strongest** of its four references, and the first trigger in the description is a scoreboard miscompare. As written, on the most common case the skill's own strongest reference is unreachable and the localisation degrades to a weaker reference or to "unreferenced". This is a one-clause fix, but it breaks the step everything downstream is seeded from, so it is a no today rather than a nearly.
remaining: BLOCKER - step 1 (line 97-99): 'Read one window of about 80 lines before it' points the only log window away from the message it tells you to record. The fatal line itself survives in the Grep output, but the expected value does not - the pack's own canonical layout in _shared/failure-signature-schema.md puts 'expected N got N' on the line AFTER the marker line, which carries no marker and so is matched by neither the Grep nor a window lying before it. That value is step 5's strongest of four references and the description's first trigger is a scoreboard miscompare.
